site.name: solstice-bank
site.summary: solstice-bank-clone Fictional digital bank "Solstice Bank" account-opening flow, aimed at the freelancer segment. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Landing: hero (with two decorative credit cards) + three value props + "Materials to prepare" checklist + top CTA to apply | | `apply.html` | Single-page 8-step linear account-opening flow with section switching: 1 eligibility + ToS / 2 personal info (name, DOB, masked SSN) / 3 contact and US address / 4 employment and income (incl. freelance / self-employed) / 5 ID verification (front/back photo upload mock + modal liveness 3-2-1 countdown) / 6 risk questionnaire (5 questions, with soft warning when compared against income) / 7 funding choice (link external bank mock OAuth, mailed check, fund later) + 4 fictional banks / 8 review (each section has Edit to jump back). Top progress bar + step dots (completed steps clickable to go back, unfinished locked). Save & continue later, Cancel application second-confirmation. Bottom-right floating Help drawer with copy that changes per step. | | `confirmation.html` | Application submission success: animated checkmark + random application number `SOL-2026-XXXX-XX` + next-step

run_plan.goal: Explore and critique the full Solstice Bank account-opening experience end to end, with deepest coverage on the 8-step onboarding flow and supporting recovery, review, and confirmation states.
run_plan.summary: Begin on the marketing landing page to validate the handoff into application start, then spend most of the run inside apply.html exercising each visible step, navigation rule, and recovery path. Prioritize states explicitly indicated in the prescan: validation errors, save-later, cancel confirmation, help drawer behavior, step-progress navigation, ID verification modal, funding options, and review-step edits. Finish by confirming successful submission to confirmation.html and repeat the highest-risk path on mobile, especially areas already flagged for small tap targets.
assumptions: apply.html contains a single-page scripted 8-step form where sections are shown/hidden rather than navigating to separate HTML files.
The 3 dialogs seen in prescan likely correspond to ID/liveness and confirmation-style overlays such as cancel/save actions.
Completed step dots are intended to be clickable for backward navigation, while unfinished steps remain locked.
The floating Help control is present throughout the application flow and its content changes by step.
Top-nav links on index.html with href '#' may be non-functional or anchor-like; they should be checked but are not expected to lead to additional pages.
risk_hotspots: index.html header nav and CTA tap sizes on mobile; several controls are already below 44px guidance
apply.html step 1 eligibility/ToS gating and inline error summary ('Please fix the following:') behavior
apply.html progress bar and step dots: lock state for unfinished steps, back-navigation for completed steps
apply.html masked SSN and DOB fields in About you step
apply.html contact/address inputs for required-field handling and data persistence between steps
apply.html employment/income logic, especially freelancer/self-employed option relevance to the product positioning
apply.html ID verification step: front/back upload mock and liveness modal 3-2-1 countdown
apply.html risk questionnaire with soft warning when answers conflict with income
apply.html funding step: choice switching among external bank OAuth mock, mailed check, and fund later; fictional bank selections
apply.html review step Edit links that jump back to prior sections without losing data
apply.html Save & continue later control and Cancel application second-confirmation flow
apply.html floating Help drawer content changes per step and does not obstruct primary actions
confirmation.html random application reference format SOL-2026-XXXX-XX and return-home path

phases.title: Landing page and entry validation
phases.objective: Confirm the marketing page communicates prerequisites clearly and provides a reliable entry into the application flow on desktop before deep form testing.
key_checks: Verify both primary entry CTAs ('Open an account' and 'Start application') navigate to apply.html
Check whether header links with '#' behave inertly, scroll, or create confusing dead interactions
Review above-the-fold clarity of value proposition, required materials checklist, and timing expectations before form start
Note mobile-relevant risks already flagged by prescan for small nav/CTA tap targets
exit_criteria: At least one CTA successfully enters apply.html
Header interaction behavior is understood and documented
Initial desktop UX issues and mobile tap-target concerns on landing are captured

phases.title: Early-step gating and validation behavior
phases.objective: Test the start of the onboarding flow for required-consent gating, validation messaging, and baseline usability of the first half of the form.
key_checks: Attempt Continue on step 1 with incomplete eligibility/consent selections to trigger and inspect the error summary and field-level cues
Complete step 1 and validate progress indicator updates appropriately
Exercise step 2 personal information inputs, including DOB and masked SSN behavior
Exercise step 3 contact/address fields with a mix of empty and completed states to verify validation and recovery
Exercise step 4 employment/income selections, including freelance/self-employed-relevant paths where visible
Check that Auto-saved messaging is credible by moving between steps and confirming entered data persists
exit_criteria: Steps 1 through 4 have been completed at least once
Validation behavior has been observed on at least two distinct steps
Data persistence across back/forward movement is confirmed or failure is documented

phases.title: Identity, risk, and contextual assistance
phases.objective: Probe the highest-complexity interactive states in the middle of the application, especially modal flows, warnings, and assistance.
key_checks: Open and complete or dismiss the ID verification front/back upload mock states
Launch the liveness check modal and observe the 3-2-1 countdown sequence, close behavior, and return-to-form state
Complete the risk questionnaire and intentionally create a mismatch scenario to surface the soft warning tied to income
Open the floating Help drawer on multiple steps and confirm the copy changes contextually without blocking form completion
Check keyboard/focus or interaction continuity after closing dialogs if practical within the run
exit_criteria: ID verification and liveness modal behavior has been directly observed
At least one soft warning state in the risk step has been triggered or ruled out
Help drawer behavior has been sampled on multiple different steps

phases.title: Funding, review, and recovery paths
phases.objective: Validate decision-heavy late-flow behavior, especially choice switching, review/edit loops, and explicit interruption controls.
key_checks: Exercise each visible funding choice: external bank mock OAuth, mailed check, and fund later
If bank linking exposes the four fictional banks, verify selection feedback and ability to switch or back out
Reach the review step and use Edit links to jump back into earlier sections, then return to review with prior data intact
Test Save & continue later and record resulting feedback/state even if it is mock-only
Test Cancel application and the second-confirmation safeguard, including backing out of cancellation
exit_criteria: All visible funding options have been visited
Review/Edit loop has been exercised for at least two earlier sections
Both save-later and cancel-confirmation interruption paths have been observed

phases.title: Submission, confirmation, and mobile regression pass
phases.objective: Complete the application to success, then rerun the most critical path on mobile to catch responsive and tap-target issues.
key_checks: Submit from review and verify navigation to confirmation.html
Confirm presence and formatting of the generated application reference and clarity of next-step messaging
Use 'Back to home' to verify return path to index.html
On mobile viewport, repeat landing-to-apply entry, first-step consent interactions, help drawer access, progress navigation, one modal interaction, and final CTA/tap-target usability
Pay special attention on mobile to the already flagged small header/link targets and any overlap from the floating Help control
exit_criteria: Confirmation content and return-home path are validated
A focused mobile pass covers landing, start of form, one complex modal, and one late-stage action

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 3 known HTML pages, with repeated visits to apply.html for both primary and recovery flows.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the majority of visible controls on apply.html, including all 8 steps, progress navigation, help drawer, validation states, ID/liveness modal behavior, funding choices, review edits, save-later, cancel confirmation, submission, and confirmation return path.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the critical path from landing into early application steps plus at least one modal and one late-stage control on mobile, with explicit checks for small tap targets, overlay interference, and progress usability.

notes: Because the site is a local demo with no network errors in prescan, prioritize client-side state changes and UX consistency over backend realism.
The run should avoid over-investing in index.html since the primary UX value and risk are concentrated in the single-page onboarding flow.
If time remains within the step budget, revisit apply.html from a fresh start once to compare clean-state behavior versus resumed/backtracked behavior.
